+experiment_id: e0-browsergym-base-qwen3-1_7b
+description: "E0: the untrained reference. Same model, same two eval splits, same seeds and the same per-turn budget as e27, with no LoRA adapter - the protocol's no-training baseline that every later condition is read against. It exists as its own config rather than as `eval.runner --config e27... --base-model` because that path writes into `runs/<experiment_id>/` regardless of whether an adapter was loaded (runner.py:36,51) and would overwrite e27's report and episode files. e27 raised a question this settles: on its held_out families the trained policy reads 0.780 success against probe numbers of 0.60 and 0.80, and on the shifted families 0.790 against probe numbers of 0.85 and 1.00 - so training appears to have helped where it trained and hurt where it did not. That comparison is not sound as it stands, because the probes ran 20 episodes per family at seed_offset 300000 while these splits are 100 episodes at 100000 and 200000. Running the identical splits under the identical geometry makes it paired seed for seed, which is the only form in which a transfer claim can be made. Run with `python -m eval.runner --config <this> --base-model`."
+seed: 42
+
+model:
+  slug: qwen3-1.7b
+  lora_r: 16
+  max_seq_length: 8192
+  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.30
+

+  # copied from e27 so the two evals differ in exactly one thing, the adapter.
+  mode: agentic
+  env: browsergym
+  env_config:
+    benchmark: miniwob
+    tasks: [click-menu-2, click-dialog-2]
+    # Must be up before launch and does not survive a box restart:
+    #   cd /workspace/miniwob-plusplus/miniwob/html && python3 -m http.server 8080

+    max_turns: 8
+  env_server:
+    repo_path: /workspace/OpenEnv/envs
+    port: 8000
+  max_prompt_length: 4096
+
+rewards:
+  compose_method: naive_sum
+  env_reward:
+    enabled: true
+    weight: 1.0
+
+eval:
+  temperature: 0.0
+  do_sample: false
+  # Pinned to e27's value. Left to derive, `max_seq - max_prompt_length` would
+  # give the same 4096 here, but pinning it means a later change to the training
+  # geometry cannot silently move the baseline out from under the comparison.
+  max_new_tokens: 4096
+  agentic:
+    splits:
+      - name: held_out
+        n_episodes: 100
+      - name: shifted
+        n_episodes: 100
+        env_config:
+          tasks: [navigate-tree, click-checkboxes-transfer]
+        seed_offset: 200000

Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

experiment_id: e0-browsergym-base-qwen3-1_7b
description: "E0: the untrained reference. Same model, same two eval splits, same seeds and the same per-turn budget as e27, with no LoRA adapter - the protocol's no-training baseline that every later condition is read against. It exists as its own config rather than as `eval.runner --config e27... --base-model` because that path writes into `runs/<experiment_id>/` regardless of whether an adapter was loaded (runner.py:36,51) and would overwrite e27's report and episode files. e27 raised a question this settles: on its held_out families the trained policy reads 0.780 success against probe numbers of 0.60 and 0.80, and on the shifted families 0.790 against probe numbers of 0.85 and 1.00 - so training appears to have helped where it trained and hurt where it did not. That comparison is not sound as it stands, because the probes ran 20 episodes per family at seed_offset 300000 while these splits are 100 episodes at 100000 and 200000. Running the identical splits under the identical geometry makes it paired seed for seed, which is the only form in which a transfer claim can be made. Run with `python -m eval.runner --config <this> --base-model`."
seed: 42

model:
  slug: qwen3-1.7b
  lora_r: 16
  max_seq_length: 8192
  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.30

training:
  # Present for the env geometry only; nothing trains here. Every value below is
  # copied from e27 so the two evals differ in exactly one thing, the adapter.
  mode: agentic
  env: browsergym
  env_config:
    benchmark: miniwob
    tasks: [click-menu-2, click-dialog-2]
    # Must be up before launch and does not survive a box restart:
    #   cd /workspace/miniwob-plusplus/miniwob/html && python3 -m http.server 8080
    miniwob_url: http://localhost:8080/miniwob/
    max_turns: 8
  env_server:
    repo_path: /workspace/OpenEnv/envs
    port: 8000
  max_prompt_length: 4096

rewards:
  compose_method: naive_sum
  env_reward:
    enabled: true
    weight: 1.0

eval:
  temperature: 0.0
  do_sample: false
  # Pinned to e27's value. Left to derive, `max_seq - max_prompt_length` would
  # give the same 4096 here, but pinning it means a later change to the training
  # geometry cannot silently move the baseline out from under the comparison.
  max_new_tokens: 4096
  agentic:
    splits:
      - name: held_out
        n_episodes: 100
      - name: shifted
        n_episodes: 100
        env_config:
          tasks: [navigate-tree, click-checkboxes-transfer]
        seed_offset: 200000
